extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the principal definitions and structural criteria from a graduate-level textbook chapter on generic smoothness, the Kleiman–Bertini theorem, depth, Cohen–Macaulayness, Miracle Flatness, and Serre's R1+S2 normality criterion. Useful for readers implementing or checking these algebraic-geometric conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic smoothness on the source (Theorem 25.3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let k be a field of characteristic 0, and let π : X → Y be a dominant morphism of integral k-varieties. Then there is a nonempty (dense) open set U ⊂ X such that π|U is smooth of dimension dim X − dim Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key ingredients in the textbook proof: consider relative dimension n = dim X − dim Y; K(X)/K(Y) is finitely generated of transcendence degree n, so Ω_{X/Y} has rank n at the generic point; use upper semicontinuity of fiber rank of a coherent sheaf and generic flatness to obtain a dense open where Ω_{X/Y} is locally free of rank n and flat, hence smooth. This result uses char k = 0 essentially (separable generation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic smoothness on the target (Theorem 25.3.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose π : X → Y is a morphism of k-varieties with char k = 0 and X smooth over k. Then there exists a dense open subset U ⊂ Y such that π|_{π^{-1}(U)} is a smooth morphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof strategy: reduce to Y smooth, consider rank loci X_r where rank(Ω_{Y/k} → Ω_{X/k}) ≤ r, use Chevalley and a dimension bound lemma (Lemma 25.3.4) to remove bad locus π(X_{n−1}), where n = dim Y. Note π^{-1}(U) may be empty if π is not dominant. Uses char 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rank-locus dimension bound (Lemma 25.3.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: For π : X → Y a morphism of finite type k-schemes with char k = 0, define X_r = {p ∈ X : rank(Ω_{Y/k}|_{π(p)} → Ω_{X/k}|_p) ≤ r}. Then dim π(X_r) ≤ r.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to control the dimension of the image of bad loci in proofs of generic smoothness and Kleiman–Bertini. Proof reduces to linear algebra at cotangent spaces and applies generic smoothness on the source after replacing Y by a smooth open.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kleiman–Bertini Theorem (25.3.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose X is a homogeneous space for a group variety G over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic 0. Let α: Y → X and β: Z → X be morphisms from smooth k-varieties Y and Z. (a) There is a nonempty open V ⊂ G such that for every σ ∈ V(k), the translate Y^σ ×_X Z is smooth of dimension dim Y + dim Z − dim X. (b) There is a nonempty open V ⊂ G such that the family (G ×_k Y) ×_X Z → V is a smooth morphism of relative dimension dim Y + dim Z − dim X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: generically a translate meets transversely. Proof uses equivariance and generic smoothness on the target twice; reduction to showing a certain G-equivariant morphism is smooth over a dense open subset, then transitivity spreads smoothness everywhere. Think of classical Bertini as a special case (hyperplane sections). Hypotheses include char 0 and homogeneous/transitive G-action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristic p counterexamples and caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Several results above (generic smoothness / Kleiman–Bertini) use char k = 0 in an essential way; the statements can fail in positive characteristic. Example: the purely inseparable extension F_p(t)/F_p(t^p) obstructs generic smoothness; one-dimensional linear series can fail to be regular in characteristic p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always check characteristic hypotheses. Exercises and examples in the text illustrate explicit failures in positive characteristic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of depth (26.1.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose (A,m) is a Noetherian local ring and M a finitely generated A-module. The depth of M (depth M) is the length of the longest M-regular sequence with elements in m. (More generally there is I-depth for an ideal I.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important immediate equivalent characterizations: depth M = 0 iff every element of m is a zero-divisor on M iff m is an associated prime of M (Exercise 26.1.A). Practical computation: successively choose non-zerodivisors in m and reduce M by them until none exist (26.1.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximal regular sequences have the same length (Theorem 26.1.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For M a finitely generated module over a Noetherian local ring (A,m), all maximal M-regular sequences contained in m have the same length. Thus depth M is the length of any maximal M-regular sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proved using the cohomological criterion (Theorem 26.1.3). This justifies algorithms that build regular sequences: any maximal chain has the correct length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohomological criterion for regular sequences (Theorem 26.1.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For (A,m) Noetherian local and M finitely generated, the following are equivalent: (i) For every finitely generated A-module N of finite length, Ext^i_A(N,M)=0 for all i < n. (ii) Ext^i_A(A/m,M)=0 for all i < n. (iii) There exists an M-regular sequence in m of length n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a cohomological characterization of depth and is used to show uniqueness of maximal regular sequences and to bound depth via Ext vanishing. Proof uses long exact sequences for Ext and Nakayama-style arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bound on depth by dimensions of associated primes (Theorem 26.1.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: The depth of a module M is at most the minimum of dim A/p as p runs over the associated prime ideals of M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This improves the crude bound depth M ≤ dim Supp M. The key tool is Lemma 26.1.7 (Ischebeck): Ext^i_A(N,M) = 0 for i < depth M − dim Supp N, which is proved by induction on dim Supp N.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohen–Macaulay definition (26.2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Noetherian local ring (A,m) is Cohen–Macaulay (CM) if depth A = dim A. A locally Noetherian scheme is Cohen–Macaulay if all its local rings are Cohen–Macaulay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric consequences: CM schemes have no embedded points; regular local rings are CM (26.2.5), smooth k-schemes are CM. Several equivalent/inductive characterizations via slicing (26.2.8) are given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slicing criterion for Cohen–Macaulayness (Theorem 26.2.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If (A,m) is Noetherian local and x ∈ m is a non-zerodivisor, then A is Cohen–Macaulay iff A/x is Cohen–Macaulay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric interpretation: for X locally Noetherian and D an effective Cartier divisor, X CM ⇒ D CM; conversely if D CM then X is CM at points of D. Use this for inductive checks of CM-ness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Miracle Flatness (algebraic) (Theorem 26.2.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let φ: (B,n) → (A,m) be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. If A is Cohen–Macaulay, B is regular, and A ⊗_B (B/n) (the fiber) has pure dimension dim A − dim B, then φ is flat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by induction on dim B using a slicing by non-zerodivisors and the local slicing criterion for flatness. Useful criterion for establishing flatness when fibers have expected dimension and source is CM while base is regular.

rubrics_metrics.name: Miracle Flatness (geometric) (Theorem 26.2.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose π: X → Y is a morphism of equidimensional finite type k-schemes, with X Cohen–Macaulay, Y regular, and fibers of π having dimension dim X − dim Y. Then π is flat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric version of the algebraic Miracle Flatness; used frequently (e.g., in Serre duality proof). Exercise 26.2.G gives equivalent characterizations: any two of (i) π flat of relative dimension dim X − dim Y, (ii) X is CM, (iii) every fiber X_y is CM of pure dimension dim X − dim Y imply the third.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions R_k and S_k (26.3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a Noetherian ring A: property R_k means A is regular in codimension k (for every prime p of codimension ≤ k, A_p is regular). Property S_k means for every prime p, depth A_p ≥ min(k, dim A_p) (i.e., local rings are CM up to codimension k and have depth at least k thereafter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These two properties quantify 'regularity in low codimension' and 'Cohen–Macaulay up to a codimension'. They are used in Serre's criterion for normality and in checking reducedness (R0 + S1) and absence of embedded points (S1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Serre's criterion for normality (Theorem 26.3.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Noetherian ring A is normal iff it has properties R1 and S2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: normality can fail either by singularities in codimension 1 (failure of R1) or by deeper depth issues (failure of S2). Consequences: Cohen–Macaulay schemes that are regular in codimension 1 are normal; regular local rings are integrally closed as a corollary. Proof: normal ⇒ R1+S2 is straightforward; the converse uses depth and integrality arguments, Hartogs-like extension (Lemma 11.3.11), and reduction to the integral-domain case before treating the general case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional facts about Cohen–Macaulayness (26.2.13–26.2.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: The locus of Cohen–Macaulay points in a locally Noetherian scheme is open. Any localization of a Cohen–Macaulay Noetherian local ring at a prime ideal is Cohen–Macaulay. CM property is preserved under A ↦ A[x] and completions A ↦ Ā.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These properties make CM-ness checkable on closed points for quasi-compact schemes and stable under common algebraic operations; references: Matsumura and EGA/Stacks tags as cited.
